name: Long Jing Qunti Zhong
parentage: The original, native heirloom population of the West Lake region.
description: 'Long Jing Population'. This is not a single clonal cultivar but the original, genetically diverse, seed-propagated heirloom population of Long Jing tea plants. Connoisseurs often prefer it to the modern #43 clone, believing it to have a deeper, more complex, and nuanced flavor profile, though its appearance is less uniform and it buds later.
plantType: Variable, seed-propagated bushes with diverse growth habits (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows in the core, traditional production areas around West Lake in Hangzhou. It is perfectly adapted to this specific terroir over centuries of growth.
processing: The processing is identical to Long Jing #43 (pan-firing), but the skill of the tea master is even more crucial due to the variability in leaf size and moisture content from the genetically diverse bushes.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. Like all Long Jing, it is a green tea where oxidation is halted immediately by pan-firing.
roasting: No roasting. The complex toasted notes are a direct result of the skillful pan-firing process.
versatility: Specialized for pan-fired green tea. It represents the historical and most complex expression of the Long Jing style.

china: Zhejiang Province (Hangou - core West Lake scenic area)

Green Tea.West Lake Long Jing (Heirloom): The most traditional and complex expression of Long Jing. It is pan-fired in the same way as #43, but its genetic diversity yields a multi-layered flavor.

sensory.aroma: Deeper and more complex than #43, with floral and fruity notes mixed in with the classic chestnut and soybean
sensory.flavor: Multi-layered, nuanced, rich, with a longer and more complex aftertaste (huigan).
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Often thicker and fuller-bodied than #43, with a very smooth and satisfying texture. The liquor is a rich yellow-green.
